name: Synthetic data, domain randomisation and sim-to-real alignment: adversarial decoy synthesis (ROGII 8th place, +-15 ft decoys, mixed synthetic continuation), pretrain-to-alignment paradigm for geophysical AI (Gao, Wu et al., USTC 2026), domain-randomised synthetic data with ambiguity self-curation (FoundationStereo, CVPR 2025), fabricated-error synthetic pretraining (ROGII 7th place refiner), distribution alignment over realism (sim-to-real RF positioning 2026), and synthetic replay against forgetting

Pretrain-to-alignment: Hui Gao, Xinming Wu, Jiarun Yang, Zhixiang Guo, Yimin Dou (University of Science and Technology of China). FoundationStereo: B. Wen et al. (NVIDIA). ROGII 7th place team. Pretrain-to-alignment: paper states source code on GitHub and baseline RGT predictions on Zenodo (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.18910332). FoundationStereo: https://github.com/NVlabs/FoundationStereo (code, weights, FSD dataset). evidence_level: Competition writeups with ablations (8th, 7th; numbers taken from our A17 extraction because Kaggle pages are JS-rendered and could not be re-fetched); arXiv preprint for pretrain-to-alignment (qualitative gains only in the summary read); peer-reviewed CVPR for FoundationStereo; code audit of our Simulator and training loop for this report (config defaults, finetune stage, run logs).
extreme_summary: Synthetic wells only help if they reproduce the real failure mode: the 8th-place U-Net broke a 6.6 plateau by (a) generating surfaces in u = TVT + Z space with real piecewise-linear statistics and injecting adversarial decoy matches at +-15 ft (decoy_prob 0.25), and (b) keeping 50% synthetic data during real training instead of pretrain-then-finetune. Geophysical pretrain-to-alignment (USTC 2026) adds a real-data alignment stage with frozen backbone + LoRA and label-free physical losses, then per-sample adaptation. Our generator already mixes ~75% synthetic throughout and has an unused real-emphasis finetune stage, but has no decoy / hard repeated-layer mode, and our one attempt to make synthetics more diverse (rb_v2_synth) hurt.
task_definition: Improve a model trained mostly on simulated examples so that it generalises to real data: by making simulations harder or more realistic where the model fails (decoys, fabricated confident errors), by randomising nuisance factors (domain randomisation), by removing or keeping ambiguous samples (self-curation), and by adding a real-data alignment stage (fine-tuning, LoRA refinement with physics losses, mixed continuation).
inputs: 8th: real trajectory and real GR residual/missingness preserved; synthetic surface u_new from the RDP skeleton of a real surface; GR rendered from the typewell at TVT = u - Z. Pretrain-to-alignment: 4,000 labelled synthetic seismic images + 3,000 unlabelled field images. Ours: real trajectory (Z), real typewell (773 typewells / ~60 master systems), synthetic TVT path from diff-block bootstrap of real paths, GR = typewell(TVT_sim) + residual noise (TVT_bias_v2 by default; real_block optional).
target_parameterisation: 8th: surfaces generated in u = TVT + Z space (A-space), TVT = u - Z. Ours: TVT path generated directly (z_shift adds a sampled trend to TVT at the heel; Ruby's z_shift keeps TVT + Z consistent, per CLAUDE.md), labels exact for synthetic wells. Pretrain-to-alignment: relative geologic time (RGT) volumes.
output_representation: Unchanged by synthetic data; the model keeps its per-column softmax over 400 TVT levels with expectation decode.
architecture: Data-side methods; architecture-agnostic. 8th U-Net leg: smp ResNet34 U-Net, 9 channels, InstanceNorm, column-wise CE; 200 epochs synthetic-only, then 50 epochs real 50% + synthetic 50% (lr 3e-5, frozen BN stats, hflip 0.5, anchor-real-prob 0.2). Pretrain-to-alignment: MAE ViT encoder pretrained on field data -> ViT encoder + conv decoder supervised on synthetic (MSE + MS-SSIM) -> frozen backbone + LoRA refined on field data with label-free geological losses -> per-sample adaptation. 7th: refiner U-Net pretrained on ~6,000 synthetic wells whose first-pass input is truth plus a lognormal-amplitude low-passed random walk (fabricated confident errors), finetuned 8 epochs on real.
core_mechanism: (1) Hard-case synthesis: a decoy is a segment where the lateral GR is rendered from the typewell at TVT +- 15 ft (the dominant aliasing period of the Eagle Ford typewells) while the label stays at the true TVT, so the network learns that a locally better GR match at the adjacent repeated band is not sufficient evidence to jump -- exactly the wrong_mode / blend failure. (2) Mixed continuation: keeping synthetic at 50% during the real stage acts as a regulariser and avoids forgetting the broad synthetic prior (the same finding as replay against catastrophic forgetting). (3) A-space generation: dip statistics (segment median ~98 ft, AR(1) slope rho ~0.248, jumps 3.1%) are realistic by construction and rejection keeps drift inside the real envelope. (4) Alignment: when field labels are scarce, adapt only small modules (LoRA) with physically motivated label-free losses on real data (orientation alignment, isochron consistency, horizon consistency), then per-sample. (5) Distribution alignment matters more than realism or size (RF positioning 2026). (6) FoundationStereo removes ambiguous samples (repetitive texture) from its randomised data -- the opposite choice to decoys; for an RMSE-expectation decode with exact synthetic labels, ambiguous samples teach calibrated hedging and should be kept, while samples whose label is wrong should be removed.
training_objective: Unchanged supervised losses on synthetic samples (our soft CE to typewell targets + expectation regression + GR_penalty). Alignment stage options: real-only or real-weighted supervised finetune (our finetune_epochs stage), LoRA/adapter refinement, or label-free consistency losses (pretrain-to-alignment) -- our GR_penalty (lateral GR vs typewell GR at predicted TVT) is already such a label-free physical loss and could be applied to unlabelled suffixes.
metric_consistent_decode: Not applicable directly; decoys with exact labels push the network toward calibrated bimodal posteriors on genuinely ambiguous wells, which the expectation decode handles optimally for RMSE. Self-curation that deletes ambiguous samples would make the model overconfident on them.
prefix_conditioning: 8th: anchor-real-prob 0.2 (real heel anchoring in synthetic). Ours: synthetic wells keep the real prefix (GR_sim[seen] = GR[seen] when range_shift == 0) and GR_calibration uses the prefix; the pretrain-to-alignment stage-4 per-sample adaptation corresponds to B10.
propose_vs_select: Not applicable; a better-trained member slots into the existing ensemble / distillation unchanged.
physical_constraints: 8th: TVT = u - Z with u piecewise linear and rejection outside the real drift envelope (<= 12 resamples). Ours: z_shift preserves TVT + Z consistency; fault_ratio 0.05 with up to 3 faults (std 1.75 ft); safe_range_guard off by default.
dataset: ROGII Kaggle: 773 wells (we use 618 train / 155 holdout). 8th: synthetic surfaces from fold-local real surfaces. Pretrain-to-alignment: global shelf-edge clinothems, 4,000 synthetic + 3,000 field seismic images. FoundationStereo: ~1M synthetic stereo pairs (FSD).
synthetic_to_real: Ours (code audit): sim_cfg['z_shift']['apply_prob'] = 0.75 in both experiments/arch and experiments/bilzard seq_NN_cfg.py and in results/0801_V2 (CLAUDE.md states 0.85 -- discrepancy to resolve); reverse_path 0.25 and GR_noise_shift 0.1 applied independently, so ~81% of samples are modified by z_shift or reverse_path; keep_ori_path 0.0; switch_typewell, typewell_mirror, xy_shift, start_point_shift all 0.0; synthetic ratio constant through training (no pretrain-only phase, no ramp-down). A real-emphasis alignment stage already exists in seq_NN_train.py (finetune_epochs, finetune_lr_reduce 0.3, finetune_disabled_augs=['z_shift'], restarts from the best checkpoint) but finetune_epochs=None in every logged run (all seq_nn.log files show finetune_epochs=None), so it has never been measured. 8th: synthetic-only 200 epochs gives zero-shot 7.62; pretrain -> real finetune plateaued at ~6.6; mixed continuation at synth_prob 0.5 broke it (f0 7.41 -> 6.92, f1 6.76 -> 6.50, f2 5.39 -> 5.23; fold 0 later 5.06); pretraining seed is a lottery uncorrelated with pretrain validation (9.08 -> 6.50 by re-rolling). 22nd: donor-relocation synthetic wells gave +-0.00. 14th: 10 synthetic pretrain epochs then mixed training with synthetic probability ~0.5 [uncertain].
metric_and_performance: 8th: U-Net stratified CV 6.437 / group 6.847; plateau-break gains 0.16-0.49 ft per fold from decoys + mixed continuation (combined, not ablated separately [uncertain]); final private gold 8th. 7th: refiner on fabricated-error synthetics 5.301 -> 5.209 CV. Pretrain-to-alignment: qualitative improvements (continuity, unconformities, steep strata); field loss 0.154 while synthetic loss stays ~0.006. Ours: Idea 2 bundle rb_v2_synth (trajectory mixup + master re-skinning at 0.5 + real_block residuals) 5.5241 vs 5.1618 at 60 ep (+0.362) and 5.1250 vs 4.9785 at 150 ep (+0.147, 19% bootstrap improving) -- harder/more diverse synthetics were NOT a free win; with TTA rb_v2_synth weights gained -0.153 ft, the largest TTA gain seen.
comparability: 8th-place fold RMSEs are on their scale (CV 6.4-6.8 for the U-Net) and not directly comparable to our 4.84-5.47 ft on 155 holdout wells; relative gains (~0.2-0.5 ft) are the transferable quantity.
validation_protocol: 8th: stratified and group (MeanShift spatial) folds; synthetic generated fold-locally to avoid leaking holdout surfaces. Ours: one random 80/20 split; synthetic wells are generated from training wells only; note the Idea 2 master-typewell bank is built from all loaded wells in-process -- verify it excludes holdout typewells [uncertain].
repeated_layers: Central. Our synthetic GR is typewell(TVT_sim) + residual noise whose TVT-bias component is small (TVT_bias_v2_tvt_std 0.95 ft), so the lateral GR almost always matches the TRUE band best; the only repeated-band ambiguity the network sees in synthetic data is the one intrinsic to the typewell. Real laterals often match an adjacent band better over hundreds of feet (22nd: lateral vs master corr 0.865, ~12 API scatter). The decoy mode injects exactly this: an adversarial segment where the wrong band is the better local match, teaching the network to keep mass on the anchored band unless evidence persists. This targets wrong_mode (24%) and blend (15%) directly.
drift: A-space generation (8th) gives realistic dip statistics; our diff-block bootstrap of real TVT paths (lengths 1024/2048/4096 rows, weights 0.45/0.40/0.15) plus optional drift_ratio (0.0 default) already reuses real path shapes. Generating in A = TVT + Z space would make synthetic drift consistent with the real one-straight-line-per-well error mode (see A18).
uncertainty_and_calibration: Synthetic data shape the prior over ambiguity: if synthetic wells are easier than real ones (no decoys), the network's posteriors are over-confident on real ambiguous wells, which raises RMSE under the expectation decode. Checkable: compare reliability curves / ECE of band-weight on synthetic validation wells vs real holdout wells (posterior_analysis.py). A real-only alignment stage mainly recalibrates.
where_to_use: Simulator.z_shift / Simulator.process in kaggle_1st_place/solution/experiments/arch/seq_NN_dataset.py (new decoy step after GR_sim is rendered), sim_cfg in experiments/arch/seq_NN_cfg.py (new 'decoy' block, synthetic ratio), and the existing finetune stage in seq_NN_train.py (finetune_epochs / finetune_disabled_augs). Distillation: the FastViT student inherits any teacher improvement and can itself be trained on decoy data.
error_mode_targeted: Band confusion (~51%: wrong_mode 24%, blend 15%, multimodal_miss 12%) via decoys; drift (~25%) via A-space generation; calibration of broad humps (~13%) via a real-data alignment stage.
gap_vs_our_implementation: Already done: heavy synthetic mixing throughout training (~75% z_shift, not pretrain-then-finetune, i.e. the regime the 8th place found best), real trajectories and typewells, real residual banks (real_block), trajectory mixup and master-series re-skinning (Idea 2, net negative so far), TVT + Z consistency. Missing: (1) no decoy / adversarial repeated-band mode -- nothing renders GR from the wrong band while keeping the true label; (2) no A-space (surface) generator with RDP skeleton + AR(1) slope deviations and drift-envelope rejection (diff-block bootstrap is path-space); (3) the real-emphasis finetune stage exists but was never run (finetune_epochs=None everywhere), and there is no ablation of the synthetic ratio (0.75 is inherited, never swept; keep_ori_path has a sweep grid (0.0, 0.025, 0.05) in seq_NN_cfg.py but no results reported); (4) no calibration comparison between synthetic and real validation; (5) no label-free alignment losses on unlabelled real suffixes (pretrain-to-alignment stage 3) -- although GR_penalty already implements one; (6) CLAUDE.md lead 2 (re-apply GR_calibration after reskin) still open, which is a sim-to-real statistics mismatch of exactly the kind the RF paper warns about.
proposed_experiment: E1 (decoys, highest priority): add sim_cfg['decoy'] = {apply_prob: 0.25, period_ft: 15 or 'acf', seg_len_ft: (200, 800), n_max: 2, blend: (0.6, 1.0)} and a Simulator.decoy step applied only to z_shift-simulated wells: pick a random suffix segment, compute the typewell's dominant autocorrelation period P near the segment's TVT (fallback 15 ft), and replace GR_sim on that segment with typewell(TVT_sim +- P) + the same residual noise (blend weight w from the range, cosine-tapered edges), leaving TVT labels unchanged. Train 150 epochs vs the 150-epoch baseline (4.9785) with seed-matched control; report pooled RMSE (seq_NN_robust_compare.py, paired bootstrap, k*) and the wrong_mode / blend / multimodal_miss shares via posterior_analysis.py on a posterior dump. Also a dose sweep at 60 epochs (apply_prob 0.1 / 0.25 / 0.4). E2 (alignment stage, zero new code): rerun the best config with finetune_epochs = 10 and 20 (z_shift disabled, lr x0.3) from the best checkpoint, plus a variant that keeps z_shift at 0.3 during finetune (mixed continuation, 8th-style) by setting finetune_disabled_augs=[] and overriding apply_prob; control = same checkpoint without finetune. E3 (synthetic ratio): z_shift apply_prob 0.5 vs 0.75 vs 0.9 at 150 epochs (2 seeds each if budget allows). E4 (A-space generator): new sample_model 'surface_rdp' in TrendSampler: u = TVT + Z of a real training well, RDP skeleton (eps 2 ft), add piecewise-linear deviations (segment length ~ lognormal median 98 ft, AR(1) slope rho 0.25, jump prob 3%), TVT = u - Z, reject if outside the real drift envelope; compare against diff_block_bootstrap. E5 (calibration check, no training): dump posteriors on 155 synthetic validation wells and on the real holdout, compare band-weight reliability; if synthetic is much better calibrated, prioritise E1/E2.
implementation_effort: E1 low-medium (~80 lines in the Simulator plus config validation). E2 low (flags exist). E3 low (config). E4 medium (new sampler mode and rejection). E5 low (posterior dump script exists).
gpu_cost: Each arm is one standard training run: ~5 h per 150-epoch ConvNeXt run on the RTX 5060 8 GB (per CLAUDE.md), ~2 h at 60 epochs; finetune arms add 10-20 epochs (~20-40 min). Decoy rendering is CPU-side and negligible. No inference cost.
distillation_compatibility: Fully compatible: better teacher posteriors propagate through KD; the student's KD batches are already 75-85% synthetic, so decoy samples also directly teach the student to hedge.
error_correlation_with_ours: A decoy-trained model should differ from the baseline mainly on repeated-band wells (the tail that dominates pooled RMSE), so it is a more diverse blend member than a second seed; a finetuned copy of the same run is highly correlated.
risk: (1) Our Idea 2 bundle (more diverse synthetics) hurt by +0.15-0.36 ft, so synthetic changes can easily worsen results; decoys at too high a rate may broaden humps (+13% error mode) or teach the model to ignore genuine band changes (faults). (2) 8th-place gains mixed decoys with a changed schedule; the decoy effect alone is not isolated [uncertain]. (3) +-15 ft is specific to Eagle Ford aliasing; other master systems need their own period (use the typewell autocorrelation). (4) Real-only finetune can forget the synthetic prior and overfit 618 wells (8th: pretrain -> finetune plateaued); prefer mixed continuation. (5) Seed lottery: 8th saw 9.08 -> 6.50 by re-rolling the pretraining seed, and our noise floor is +-0.39 ft, so single-seed comparisons are weak; use 2 seeds for decisive arms. (6) The 0.75 vs 0.85 synthetic-ratio discrepancy between code and notes should be resolved before interpreting ratio sweeps.
notes: Decoys vs self-curation is the key design choice: FoundationStereo deletes ambiguous samples because in its data the ambiguity makes labels unlearnable for a mode-seeking metric (EPE/bad-pixel); in our RMSE-expectation setting with exact synthetic labels, ambiguity is the signal the model must learn to hedge on, so we should ADD ambiguous (decoy) samples and only delete synthetic samples whose label is physically implausible. Pretrain-to-alignment's stage 3 (frozen backbone + LoRA, label-free geological losses on field data) maps to training a small adapter with GR_penalty on unlabelled suffix GR of holdout/test wells (transductive), which is closer to B10. Related items: A17 (8th/7th/22nd writeups), A18 (A-space identity), A19 (external typelogs to diversify masters), B09 (calibration), B10 (per-sample adaptation).
